newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr steady vs yen, Aussie weak after job data.
newsitem.headline: Dlr steady vs yen, Aussie weak after job data.

text.p: *Dollar locked in narrow range against yen in morning Tokyo amid lack of fresh factors, with downside supported on Japanese investors' buying interest.
*Australian dollar weakened against the U.S. dollar and yen after release of Australian employment data.

*Australia's seasonally adjusted estimate of the number of employed persons rose 11,900 in June to 8.392 million, against 8.380 million in May. Ecomonist had on average expected employment to rise by around 40,250 people in June.
*Australian dollar fell to US$0.7410/15, compared with US$0.7439/44 just before jobs report. Aussie/yen stood at 83.56/66 yen at 0146 GMT, compared with around 83.79/89 yen before employment data.
*Profit-taking took greenback down versus mark, while short-covering buoyed mark/yen rate. Mark/yen at 64.11/14 yen at 0153 GMT against 64.06 yen at Wednesday's New York close.

*Many participants in market await Bank of England decision on interest rates at two-day monetary policy meeting, which ends later on Thursday. They said BOE is expected to raise its interest rates by 25 basis points.
*Dollar hovered in narrow range versus yen in early Tokyo trade; activity limited due to lack of fresh incentives.
*Dollar/yen upside capped by Japanese exporter offers above 113 yen but downside also seen limited by investor bids.
*Talk that Japanese institutional investors and public fund bodies, who were bidding dollar at around 112.30/40 yen on Wednesday, have raised their bids to around 112.60 yen.
*Mark edged higher against yen on short-covering.
*Talk of solid mark bids around 63.80 yen, traders said.
